headline: mSecure tells users to change passwords without saying why; Barracuda root-access flaws; Node-RED exploitation continues

bullets.text: New: The Register reports password manager mSecure is telling users to change their passwords and won't say why.
Still active: BleepingComputer reports Barracuda is warning of critical flaws that allow root access to its devices.

SITCON 2 holds on a critical report. The Hacker News says attackers exploit a critical Siemens IoT2050 flaw, CVE-2026-58115, to plant remote command backdoors. Help Net Security reports the same CVE in Node-RED used to deploy a Linux bot and backdoors.

Connect Secure, 4 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13.
Binance, 7 outlets: The Register reports the FBI pins the $6.3B heist on North Korean hackers.

Breaches still active: SecurityWeek reports a Frontline Education data breach affecting over 1.3 million people. Harvard's breach, with 850,537 accounts added to Have I Been Pwned, also remains on the board.

actions: If you use mSecure, change the passwords stored in it and watch for a vendor explanation.
Inventory Barracuda devices, check the vendor's advisory for the critical root-access flaws, and apply its fixes.
Find Node-RED instances and Siemens IoT2050 devices, patch CVE-2026-58115 per vendor guidance, and look for backdoors.
Patch GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) and Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) now; both KEV due dates have passed.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
Update DSM on Synology NAS devices, restrict their internet exposure, and confirm backups are intact.
